Definition: to erect, i.e. create; by extension, to procure, especially by purchase (causatively, sell); by implication to own
BiblicalUsage: To buy is the word for paying the price: David would not take Araunah's threshingfloor for nothing, but buy it for the full price, Omri bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver. Moses asks Israel, is not He thy Father that hath bought thee.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the buying word is the thread from the marketplace to redemption, because God bought His people before they could buy anything back. What strikes me is David's refusal to offer God what cost him nothing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
